key_results: Hyperlink contribution quantified via contagion backbone; local centrality metrics effectively rank high-contributing hyperlinks; performance varies with diffusion parameters
comments: Theoretical framework is solid but experimental validation limited to face-to-face contact networks; generalization to other domains unclear.

model_io.model: Susceptible-Infectious threshold process on temporal higher-order networks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Local hyperlink properties effectively predict high-contribution hyperlinks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; centrality metrics correlate with infection contribution

title: Partial coherence control delivers skyrmionic topological resilience and transitions
task: Engineering partial coherence to achieve topological resilience and transitions in optical skyrmions
key_results: Spatial coherence acts as primary determinant of topological stability in stochastic fields; engineered partial coherence enables self-healing under turbulence and triggers on-demand skyrmion-skyrmionium conversion and lattice splitting
comments: Theoretically elegant extension of skyrmion physics to general partially coherent light; experimental validation in real turbulent environments remains outstanding.

model_io.model: Stochastic optical skyrmion field with engineered coherence structure

hypotheses.hypothesis: Partial coherence can preserve topology under extreme turbulence
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; engineered coherence provides self-healing mechanism

hypotheses.hypothesis: Coherence structure can trigger topological phase transitions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; on-demand skyrmion-skyrmionium conversion and lattice splitting demonstrated

title: Domain wall dynamics in trilayer sliding ferroelectric γ-InSe
task: Resolving domain wall dynamics and multistate switching in trilayer sliding ferroelectric γ-InSe
key_results: Trilayer exhibits distinct DW locations in adjacent layers separated by nonpolar domains; polarization switching proceeds through distinct kinetic stages with parabolic displacement-time relation transitioning to constant velocity; inter-DW interactions observed
comments: Atomistic DFT and ML-aided MD provide mechanistic insights, but generalization to longer multilayer stacks and experiments remains unexplored.

model_io.model: Trilayer γ-InSe sliding ferroelectric via DFT + machine-learning MD

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trilayer architecture introduces nonpolar intermediate domains unlike bilayer systems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; nonpolar domains situated between up/down-polarized ferroelectric domains

hypotheses.hypothesis: DW motion exhibits parabolic acceleration transitioning to constant velocity under field
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; coupled DW motion shows significant inter-DW interactions

title: Triple band Yagi antenna design and performance prediction for next generation (6G) wireless applications using supervised regression models
task: Designing and predicting performance of sub-THz Yagi antenna for 6G using machine learning
key_results: Compact 53 × 47 μm antenna on polyimide achieves 14.9 dB gain and 99.65% efficiency; Random Forest Regression outperforms neural networks for efficiency prediction from simulation datasets
comments: Multi-simulator validation (CST, HFSS, FEKO) is rigorous, but ML predictive models trained on simulation rather than experimental data may not generalize.

model_io.model: Sub-THz Yagi antenna with Random Forest efficiency predictor

hypotheses.hypothesis: Random Forest regression predicts antenna efficiency more accurately than neural networks
hypotheses.result: Confirmed from extensive simulation dataset

title: Wideband mmWave antenna with integrated 1 × 8 feed-array configuration for high-gain 5G wireless applications using characteristic mode theory
task: Designing wideband mmWave antenna for 5G using characteristic mode theory with 1×8 phased array
key_results: Single element: 22.5–39 GHz impedance bandwidth (53.66%); 1×8 array achieves 11–15.8 dBi gain; peak gains 12.8 dBi (28 GHz) and 15.5 dBi (38 GHz); measured and simulated results agree well
comments: CMT-guided design provides clear modal interpretation and measured prototype validation, though array gain variation across band remains moderately wide.

model_io.model: Characteristic Mode Theory-based mmWave antenna and 1×8 linear array

hypotheses.hypothesis: Characteristic mode analysis can explain wideband resonance through multiple excited modes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; modes J₃+J₁+J₄, J₃+J₄+J₅, J₃+J₂+J₄, J₂+J₃+J₅ drive resonance at 24, 28, 32, 36 GHz

title: Investigating the hydrogen storage potential and optoelectronic properties of double perovskite ZMg2FeH8 (Z = Ca, Be) hydrides
task: Evaluating hydrogen storage potential and optoelectronic properties of double perovskite hydrides
key_results: CaMg₂FeH₈ and BeMg₂FeH₈ exhibit gravimetric capacities of 5.28 and 6.63 wt% respectively; desorption temperatures 460.7 and 476.4 K; both stable as semiconductors under 0–70 GPa; significant UV absorption
comments: Comprehensive first-principles study showing promising hydrogen density, but lack of kinetics evaluation and comparison to experimental standards limits practical assessment.

model_io.model: CASTEP first-principles calculations of ZMg₂FeH₈ (Z = Ca, Be)

hypotheses.hypothesis: BeMg₂FeH₈ exhibits higher gravimetric capacity than CaMg₂FeH₈
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 6.63 vs 5.28 wt%

title: Microstructure-aware deep learning bridges atomistics to macroscale for shock-to-detonation prediction
task: Bridging molecular dynamics to continuum models for shock-to-detonation prediction using deep learning
key_results: MISTnetX CNN trained on MD captures shock-microstructure interactions and hotspot formation; enables parameter-free run-to-detonation prediction in nanostructured RDX composite without invoking equilibrium assumptions
comments: Innovative multiscale approach circumvents scale-separation limitations, but validation limited to synthetic material; real experimental comparison needed.

model_io.model: MISTnetX convolutional neural network bridging MD and FE
inputs: molecular dynamics simulations of shock propagation through microstructures
outputs: continuum FE model inputs for mechanics/chemistry/thermal transport

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deep learning can bridge atomistic and continuum scales without equilibrium assumptions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MISTnetX captures hotspot formation and deflagration-to-detonation transition

title: Exploring the influence of reverberation on the perceived quality of time-scale modified speech
task: Assessing perceived quality of time-scale modified speech with added reverberation
key_results: At 2.5× slowdown, speech with reverberation rated higher quality than without; no significant language difference (Polish vs. English); reverberation characteristics statistically significant
comments: MUSHRA-based perceptual study shows counterintuitive benefit of reverberation, though effect is limited to extreme slowdown ratios and may not generalize to other acoustic environments.

model_io.model: MUSHRA listening test protocol

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reverberation improves perceived quality of slowed speech
hypotheses.result: Confirmed at 2.5× slowdown; no effect at lower slowdown ratios

title: Polarization selective nonlinear optical enhancement in hybrid silicon metamembrane based on bound states in the continuum via symmetry engineering
task: Enhancing third harmonic generation and four-wave mixing via bound states in continuum in silicon metamembranes
key_results: Symmetry-protected BIC converted to high-Q quasi-BIC via geometry tuning; N-ANC-doped PMMA achieves largest Q-factor improvement and frequency conversion efficiency through resonance and material engineering
comments: Strong experimental-theoretical alignment demonstrating coherent design strategy, though nonlinear conversion efficiency absolute values not quantified in abstract.

model_io.model: Hybrid silicon metamembrane with air and polymeric nanoholes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Symmetry engineering can maximize Q-factor and nonlinear conversion efficiency
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; combined effects of increased Q-factor and higher χ³ yield significant FCE enhancement

title: Activity removes transport arrest and restores phase separation under geometric confinement
task: Determining how activity reshapes phase separation dynamics under geometric confinement
key_results: Self-propulsion restores particle transport and eliminates logarithmic coarsening, transitioning to power-law kinetics beyond activity threshold despite persistent confinement
comments: Elegantly connects activity-enhanced transport to phase ordering through mean-squared displacement analysis, though primarily computational/simulation-based.

model_io.model: Active particle system in confined geometry

hypotheses.hypothesis: Activity can overcome geometric barriers to transport
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; transport restoration correlates with reactivation of rapid phase ordering

hypotheses.hypothesis: Logarithmic slowdown in confined phase separation can be reversed
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; activity enables transition to power-law coarsening

title: Shape-dependent direction reversal in anisotropic catalytic microswimmers
task: Elucidating shape-dependent propulsion direction reversal in catalytic microswimmers
key_results: Discs, tori, and bent rods reverse direction with H₂O₂ concentration; spheres and side-propelling rods do not; direction determined by interplay of pH-dependent zeta potential ratio and geometry; reversible across different materials and sizes
comments: Novel experimental demonstration using 3D-printed particles, though mechanism involving substrate-induced solute confinement remains partially speculative.

model_io.model: Catalytic microswimmers with varied shapes in H₂O₂ solution
inputs: particle shape (disc, torus, bent rod, sphere)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Particle shape affects propulsion direction in catalytic swimmers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; direction reversal occurs for anisotropic shapes via pH-dependent zeta potential and geometry interplay

title: Navigating regulatory fragmentation in the convergence of synthetic biology, artificial intelligence, and automation
task: Analyze regulatory fragmentation across synthetic biology, AI, and automation convergence
key_results: Identified critical ambiguities in regulatory categorization across 16 nations; demonstrated multiplicative rather than additive regulatory friction in 7 collaboration scenarios
comments: This is a policy and governance analysis rather than a biological systems modeling paper, focusing on institutional frameworks rather than mechanistic understanding.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Regulatory friction compounds multiplicatively when synthetic biology, AI, and automation converge across jurisdictions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through cross-jurisdictional scenario analysis; proposed RIOT framework to mitigate
